content: 1. Certain medications may alter the way your drugs work or increase the risk of severe side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. It is essential to maintain a list of all the products you use, including prescription drugs, over-the-counter medications, and herbal supplements, and share this information with your doctor and pharmacist. 2. This medication may interfere with specific laboratory tests, such as urine catecholamine levels, potentially leading to inaccurate test results. 3. In the event of an overdose, if the individual exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, immediately call emergency services (911). Otherwise, contact a poison control center without delay. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. 4. This medication has been prescribed specifically for your current condition and should not be used for other purposes unless directed by your doctor. 5. While taking this medication, your doctor may order laboratory or medical tests, such as a complete blood count or kidney and liver function tests, to monitor your progress and check for side effects. 6. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. 7. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Taking expired minocycline can lead to serious illness. 8. This medication is used to treat moderate to severe acne in individuals aged 12 years and older. It works by reducing the number of pimples. Minocycline belongs to a class of drugs known as tetracycline antibiotics and treats acne caused by bacterial infections. It is not effective against viral infections such as the common cold or flu. 9. Before starting this medication, read the patient information leaflet provided by your pharmacist. Take this medication orally, with or without food, as directed by your doctor, usually once daily. Swallow the medication whole; do not crush or chew it. Take each dose with a full glass of water (8 ounces or 240 milliliters) unless otherwise directed by your doctor. Do not lie down for at least 10 minutes after taking this medication. For this reason, avoid taking it right before bedtime. 10. Take this medication 2 to 3 hours before or after consuming products containing aluminum, calcium, iron, magnesium, zinc, or bismuth subsalicylate. Examples include antacids, quinapril, sucralfate, vitamins/minerals, dairy products (such as milk and yogurt), and calcium-enriched juice. For optimal effectiveness, take this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals. Continue taking it for the full prescribed duration, even if symptoms disappear. Do not skip doses. 11. Common side effects may include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, lightheadedness, dizziness, or a sensation of spinning. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. 12. Rarely, minocycline may cause increased pressure around the brain (intracranial hypertension, or IH). Women of childbearing age who are overweight or have a history of IH are at greater risk. If IH develops, it typically resolves after stopping minocycline; however, there is a risk of permanent vision loss or blindness. 13. This medication may rarely cause a severe intestinal condition due to a bacteria called Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile). This condition may occur during treatment or weeks to months after treatment has stopped. 14. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may result in oral thrush or a new yeast infection. Inform your doctor if you notice white patches in your mouth, a change in vaginal discharge, or other new symptoms. 15. A very serious allergic reaction to this drug is rare. However, seek immediate medical attention if you experience symptoms of a severe allergic reaction, such as rash, itching/swelling (especially of the face/tongue/throat), severe dizziness, or trouble breathing. 16. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. 17. Before taking minocycline, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other tetracyclines (such as doxycycline), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. 18. This drug may cause dizziness. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate this effect. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks requiring alertness until you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. 19. This medication may increase your sensitivity to the sun. Limit your time in the sun, avoid tanning booths and sunlamps, and use sunscreen and protective clothing when outdoors. 20. Minocycline may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. Inform your healthcare provider about your vaccination history. 21. Children younger than 8 years may be more sensitive to the side effects of minocycline, particularly tooth discoloration. Tooth discoloration has also been reported in older children and young adults. 22. Inform your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. You should not become pregnant while using minocycline, as it may harm an unborn baby. This medication also passes into breast milk. 23. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription/nonprescription drugs and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. 24. This medication may interfere with certain lab tests, such as urine catecholamine levels, potentially causing false test results. Inform laboratory personnel and your doctors that you are using this drug. 25. If someone has overdosed and exhibits serious symptoms such as passing out or trouble breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. 26. This medication has been prescribed for your current condition only. Do not use it for other conditions unless directed by your doctor. 27. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Taking expired minocycline can cause serious illness. 28. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
